      "partial_result": "# Verdict: REJECT\n\n**Don't fund the 0.05 negative-column margin SmoothAP arm.** Run neither the FIT census Fable proposed nor a fresh control/candidate pair. The decisive evidence is already in the repo: this margin was effectively tested on this exact control family, and R1 netted zero.\n\nI edited no repo files, imported no Torch, and ran no SSH sessions, jobs, consultations or spawns. I did save one memory note outside the repo.\n\n## 1. The 0.05 margin has already been tested on this family\nThe `live-top1` arm in `scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py` (`live_top1_hinge`, line 907; `loss_terms`, line 917) is the same setup Fable proposes:\n- The same SmoothAP plus regression control, trained on the A/C readout only.\n- The same current canonical 6355-row gallery.\n- The same temperature, 0.01.\n- One addition: `relu(.05 + s_hardest_wrong \u2212 s_nearest_positive)`, with coefficient 1.\n\nThat hinge targets the best-positive R1 boundary directly, which is more direct than an all-positive SmoothAP shift. Results in `live-top1-first-selection-score-v1/receipt.json`, on the same 1734/1715/498 panel at seed 061:\n\n| Measure | Control | Candidate |\n|---|---|---|\n| R1 | 96.828143% | 96.828143% (2 queries gained, 2 lost, of 55 errors) |\n| mAP@R | 82.733% | 82.499% (\u22120.234 pt) |\n| Decision | | KILL |\n\nIts fixed FIT diagnostic (`evaluate_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:1727`) tracked 63 first-B64 triples. In both arms, only 1 had a margin below 0.05, and the median margin moved by only +0.0009.\n\nThat diagnostic is the precondition Fable's own rejection rule tests: \"FIT already satisfies the margin.\" It is only partial, because the triples were mined from teacher geometry rather than from each endpoint's hardest negatives, and it covers one seed and 63 anchors. Its `decision.md` already says the next step \"must change demonstrated representation or supervision cause rather than extend this loss recipe.\"\n\nFable's claim that the arm differs from every closed arm is false. It treated the \"older\" hinge as a separate recipe, but it ran on top of the accepted SmoothAP.\n\n## 2. A shifted sigmoid is not a hinge (mechanism)\nIn `smooth_ap_terms` (`train_siglip2_identity_diversity.py:1228`), adding m to the negative columns gives each pair the gradient weight \u03c3\u2032((m \u2212 g)/T)/T, where g = s_p \u2212 s_n. The margin moves the active window rather than widening it:\n\n| Pair gap g | m = 0 (fraction of peak) | m = 0.05 (fraction of peak) |\n|---|---|---|\n| +0.05 (already correct) | 2.66% | 100% |\n| 0 (tie) | 100% | 2.66% |\n| \u22120.057 (median of the core errors) | 1.33% | 0.009% |\n\n- **What the margin really does:** it reallocates FIT gradient away from real violations and ties, and toward pairs that are already correct by 0 to 0.1. \"Reactivating inert pairs to widen the exported boundary\" is a hypothesis this mechanism does not support.\n- **Prior art cuts the other way:** Liu et al., ECCV 2020 (\"Negative Margin Matters\") found that this kind of separation margin improves seen classes but hurts transfer to novel classes. The selection panel's products are disjoint from FIT, so they are novel classes. Fable's \"negative-margin\" label is the opposite of that paper's meaning; rename it \"negative-column margin\".\n- **Better-studied relatives:** ROADMAP (NeurIPS 2021) uses calibration with absolute thresholds, not a sigmoid shift. Smooth-AP (ECCV 2020) uses no margin at all.\n\n## 3. Best-positive R1 vs all-positive AP\n- The term is a mean over all positives, about 5.3 per anchor (6355 rows, 1008 products).\n- The live-top1 diagnostic shows the best positives on FIT are already separated by at least 0.05 in 62 of 63 cases.\n- So the shifted weight mainly lands on the non-best positives. That moves mAP, not R1.\n\nThis matches past results:\n- The connected candidate gained +2.30 mAP but only +0.35 R1.\n- The earlier verdict found that SmoothAP moves mAP rather than R1.\n\nThe binding gate is the paired product R1 lower bound being above zero. The connected run's interval was about \u00b10.46 pt, so passing needs roughly 8 net flipped queries per seed. Live-top1 flipped 4 queries with a net of 0.\n\nAs a descriptive check only, not usable as a gate: in the census, just 2\u20133 of the 44 shared errors per control endpoint sit within 0.01 of flipping, and 5 within 0.02.\n\n## 4. Checking the claims (I agree with all five of the root's rejections)\n\n| Claim | Status |\n|---|---|\n| The gradient is below 1% of peak at 5T | False: it is 2.659%. The 1% point is about 6T (0.06). No non-arbitrary margin follows from T alone. |\n| A step-128 ranking loss of 0.033\u20130.040 means saturation | Unsupported. Smoothing mass from many negatives within about 3T makes up the aggregate, which can't separate near-ties from violations. |\n| The core error rate q = 44/1734 can serve as a FIT quantile gate | Reject. It is held data, and a memorised FIT quantile isn't comparable with a held error rate. |\n| The cost ratio is about 1.00 | A prediction only.
